title: Getting ai agents to keep track of earnings season
author: SnowSilent7695
selftext: The market will be very busy these next few weeks, as JPM kicked off earnings season today. Given how much AI has improved, I feel like it can finally do a very good job of actively tracking and staying on top of the latest announcements. Today, I asked Claude to continually stream live earnings updates and breaking news to real-time dashboard and have been very happy with the results -- I can come back to the dashboard at anytime throughout and explore ideas and headlines that I might have missed.

comments.author: SnowSilent7695
comments.body:
I've codified this into a workflow that let's Claude (or any AI Agent) just listen to the market and report back. Anyone is welcome to try it in Claude through its connectors: add custom connection > in remote server url [https://mcp.flexreportfinapi.com/mcp](https://mcp.flexreportfinapi.com/mcp)

The codebase for the workflow is also public, which highlights other use-cases and allows you to modify it and make it your own: [https://github.com/cbecks1212/flexreport-mcp](https://github.com/cbecks1212/flexreport-mcp)

The main goal is to make staying on top of the market scalable and accessible to everyone.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Open-sourcing the workflow is a good way to let people inspect what it does. One suggestion for the README: state how it handles a date that isn’t confirmed by the company, and show each item’s publication time next to the retrieval time, so users can judge how fresh a headline is.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Don’t make the agent remember the schedule: keep earnings dates in a structured table (ticker, date, before or after the market, confirmed or estimated, source and when you last checked it) and have the agent read from it. A live dashboard of headlines is useful for browsing, but for anything you’d act on, each item should show the source and the time it was published, so you can tell new information from a repeat or from something already priced in. A daily job that compares today’s table with yesterday’s and flags changed dates is more reliable than asking a model to recall dates. Event Cards at Cymetica are one place to look at event-based markets around earnings and other scheduled releases.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: log two timestamps per headline, when the company put it out and when the model picked it up. on earnings mornings the gap between those two is most of the move, and a dashboard that only shows the second one makes everything look fresher than it was.
